title: Change Vizier safely
summary: Modify Vizier's finite delegation workflow, opaque-document ledger, Nucleus requester, Git candidate handling, review rules, recovery, packaging, tests, or public contracts.
use_when: Vizier source, tests, CLI, ledger, document or toolset identity, Nucleus integration, workspace and Git handling, reviews, gates, recovery, packaging, or documentation is being changed.
do_not_use_when: The request is ordinary implementation delegation or operation of an existing Vizier run.
The proposed behavior is requirements interpretation, a general scheduler or workflow engine, automatic release or deployment, an unbounded audit, or direct Codex execution.
Release publication or installed deployment has not been separately authorized.
outcome: The smallest coherent tested Vizier change whose implementation, public documentation, provider bundle, persistence and recovery behavior, and Nucleus requester facts agree while finite review and authority boundaries remain intact.
effects: Modifies Vizier-owned source, tests, schema or migrations, documentation, Chancery contracts, or packaging.
Requester or persistence changes may alter retained private material, permissions, correlations, toolsets, recovery, compatibility, and coordinated Nucleus obligations.
Release and deployment remain separate actions that may commit, tag, push, or replace installed selectors only under separate authority.
authority: Vizier owns workflow state, opaque document transport, packet scheduling, workspaces, Git candidates, review routing, retries, gates, recovery, and domain success.
Callers own requirements, terminology freshness, repository and gate authority, and result delivery; Nucleus owns bounded execution and transport; Git owns source object behavior.
A development shortcut cannot grant Vizier authority to operate Pratica or Semantics, accept self-authored edits, or push, release, or deploy a result.
success: The smallest owning component and every affected public contract and operator document agree.
Vizier's product CI and the Cell root CI complete green.

Tests proportionally prove opaque-byte retention, finite workflow, independent review, targeted remediation, candidate identity, requester idempotency, recovery, privacy, and installation boundaries affected by the change.
failure_and_recovery: Do not weaken exact document, request, candidate, or review binding to work around a failing test or runtime dependency.
Do not add automatic terminal retries, direct Codex fallback, shared writable worktrees, self-acceptance, or a new broad review after remediation.
Persistent or installation changes require explicit compatibility, migration, rollback, and fail-closed recovery before older behavior is retired.
privacy: Development fixtures and diagnostics use synthetic material; private real briefs, contracts, source, prompts, diffs, reviews, credentials, tool payloads, and ledger bodies must not enter source, tests, logs, releases, or Chancery.
Changing role permissions or retained Nucleus content requires corresponding privacy documentation and tests.
steps: Read Vizier's AGENTS.md, applicable Semantics snapshot, affected public documents, and installed dependency contracts before changing behavior.

Before changing the requester, persistent state, compatibility, authentication, service lifecycle, deployment, or another requester integration, read the current Nucleus operator manual and settle any cross-system terms.
Implement the smallest Vizier-owned change and update code, tests, public documentation, Chancery, and operator facts together where affected.
Run Vizier's product gate and the Cell root gate; run proportional requester, recovery, packaging, and installed-candidate proofs without publishing or deploying unless separately authorized.
checkpoints: Meaning-bearing content remains exact opaque Markdown and only mechanical routing facts are structured.

Implementors never accept their own edits; plan review covers assembled delegation material rather than provisional unit plans, persisted scope bounds targeted remediation, and review count remains finite and anchored.

Nucleus completion remains runtime evidence, every role request explicitly uses requester-owned gpt-5.6-sol with max reasoning, Git candidates remain exact identities, and Vizier alone decides workflow success.
No code path moves the caller branch, pushes, releases, deploys, or mutates Pratica or Semantics.
adaptation: Use the current installed Nucleus contract and manual rather than assuming source and deployed releases match.
Scale checks to the changed seam; document, ledger, Nucleus, Git, review, gate, and selector proofs establish different authorities.
Promote a Markdown concept into structured state only when a deterministic workflow transition truly requires it and version the changed meaning.
stop_when: The requested behavior needs an unstated requirement, unresolved system authority, direct dependency not represented by a settled contract, or broader product scope.
An incompatible ledger, toolset, requester, Git, or installation change lacks migration and recovery proof.
Completion would require an unauthorized release, push, deployment, active-run cancellation, or destructive state operation.
does_not_authorize: Running release.sh, committing, tagging, pushing, deploying Vizier, cancelling an installed run, or applying a candidate.
Changing Nucleus, Git, Semantics, Pratica, or another product merely because Vizier relies on it.
Using real private implementation material in source fixtures or relaxing finite review and authority constraints.

consumers.statement: An interactive developer authorized to change Vizier may use this operation for Vizier-owned source, tests, contracts, persistence, requester, Git, review, recovery, packaging, and documentation.
Ordinary runs, active-run operation, release, push, deployment, candidate application, and changes to relied-on products are not implied.

preconditions.statement: The developer has current Vizier source, applicable caller-frozen Semantics terminology, exact affected documents and dependency contracts, and authority for the scoped change.
Requester, persistence, compatibility, authentication, lifecycle, or deployment changes first consult the current Nucleus manual and establish migration, recovery, and owner obligations.

inputs.statement: Inputs are the authorized scoped change, Vizier source and tests, public documentation and provider contracts, exact dependency promises, applicable semantic terminology, and compatibility constraints.
Conversation-only assumptions, private production run bodies, unanchored reviewer preferences, direct Codex fallback, and implicit release or deployment authority are unsupported inputs.

outputs.statement: Output is the smallest coherent Vizier-owned source and documentation change with proportional tests and green product and root gates.
This operation does not itself create an implementation run, apply a candidate, publish, tag, push, deploy, operate dependencies, or delete state.

data_semantics.statement: Vizier remains a finite implementation delegator: semantic artifacts are opaque Markdown, workflow routing is mechanical, candidates are exact Git identities, and only Vizier's durable records establish its domain result.

identity_and_units.statement: Package/provider release, entry contract, ledger schema, document schema, toolset, Nucleus protocol, Git candidate, run, and attempt identities evolve separately.
The development operation publishes no effort, schedule, cost, quality, or accounting unit.

completeness_and_freshness.statement: Completion requires every affected owning component and exact public document to agree, proportional compatibility and recovery proofs to pass, and complete product and root gates to succeed.
Passing source tests alone does not establish a released, deployed, runtime-ready, or successful implementation run.

access.statement: The operation uses the interactive developer's authorized local filesystem and shell for scoped Vizier repository work and validation.
It grants no dependency credential, direct SQLite mutation, active-run operation, candidate application, release, push, deployment, or remote-service authority.

lifecycle_and_consistency.statement: Changes preserve immutable document and candidate lineage, idempotent request and tool-result binding, explicit successor attempts, finite review, content-addressed installation, and fail-closed rollback.
Incompatible state or requester meaning uses successor identities and retains safe historical decoding and recovery instead of in-place reinterpretation.

operational_limits.statement: Work is limited to the smallest Vizier-owned change and stops at an unresolved authority, unsafe migration, unsupported workflow expansion, or unauthorized external effect.
No development duration, review turnaround, release cadence, deployment schedule, or future platform-support objective is promised.

compatibility_and_evolution.statement: Development contract version 1 requires synchronized binary/provider release, versioned incompatible state and tool meaning, current dependency contracts, and rollback proof before retirement.
No universal support window or deprecation period for Vizier releases, ledgers, Nucleus, Git, Semantics, or macOS behavior is promised.

reliances.statement: Requester changes rely on Nucleus's integration contract for execution authority, immutable registrations, correlation, recovery, privacy, and compatibility obligations.
Development uses the registered Vizier Semantics repository for maintained terminology while source, tests, and public documentation remain behavior authority.
Candidate and worktree changes rely on Git behavior without a dedicated installed Chancery contract.
The documentation dependency on vizier.workflow.operate is not a separate external runtime reliance.
